foundations.claim: Projection of a dominated splitting and uniform scaling
reasoning: For bounded t, Df_t and Df_(-t) have uniformly bounded norms on the compact manifold. On the flow direction, |X(x_t)|/|X(x)|=||Df_t|_(span X)|| is bounded above and away from zero by those bounds. This verifies Lemma 2.1 without needing a lower bound for |X(x)| near singularities.
When X is contained in F, the projection of E to N is an isomorphism onto E_N with uniformly bounded inverse, because the angle between E and F is uniformly separated from zero.

For unit u in E_N and v in F_N, take u' in E projecting to u and v'=Df_(-t) psi_t(v) in F. Then projection(v')=v, so |v'|>=1, while |u'| is uniformly bounded. Tangent domination bounds |Df_t u'|/|Df_t v'|, and orthogonal projection cannot increase the numerator.

Since Df_t v'=psi_t v and psi_t u is the projection of Df_t u', the desired normal domination follows. The scalar speed factor in psi_t^* cancels in the ratio, so the same splitting is dominated for both normal flows.

With E perpendicular to F, E_N=E and the inverse-projection constant is one, yielding (2.8). This establishes a time-one cone statement; it does not impose an instantaneous adapted-metric inequality for every nonintegral time.

foundations.claim: Scaled flow boxes, holonomy domains and shadowing concatenation
foundations.disposition: Definitions and internal calculations checked; the cited Liao existence/regularity theorems retained as external inputs
reasoning: The relative radius is proportional to |X(x)|; it is not a uniform ordinary radius near a singularity. Proposition 2.4 supplies the uniform inverse derivative bound 3 and excludes singularities in each scaled flow box.

Recursive application of the one-step holonomy domain gives the factor K0^(-T) for integer T. Fractional time is handled by the separate short-time flow-box estimate and the time reparametrization, rather than by asserting invariance of a discrete fake foliation.

A safe choice in (2.12) uses bounds for DX as well as flow speed. On a compact manifold, d(f_t x,f_t y)<=e^(L|t|)d(x,y), while |X(x_t)|>=e^(-L|t|)|X(x)|; therefore K>=2L (with chart constants absorbed) gives the required relative inclusion.

For the time correction, write F_x^(-1)(y)=v+a X(x). The signed correction is tau_x(y)=-a=-<F_x^(-1)(y),X(x)>/|X(x)|^2. The absolute norm displayed in the proof on page 16 is not the signed time, but replacing it by this linear coefficient gives the derivative bound needed there.
Specifically, ||D tau_x||<=3/|X(x)|, and |X(x)| ||D_y tau_(x,y)(1)|| <=3||Df_1|| ||Df_(-1)||. Thus the bound (2.16) survives the signed-coordinate correction.
Scaled holonomy differentiation at the center gives psi_t^*, as in (2.18). The source's uniform scaled derivative bound is K1', distinguished from the unscaled K1.

Restriction and concatenation in Lemma 2.11 follow by subtracting the old initial reparametrization value and by concatenating increasing functions with matching endpoints. Lemma 2.12 then follows by induction over complete unit intervals and the final short interval.
The uniform existence and continuity claims of Propositions 2.4, 2.5 and 2.8 are cited from [30], [36] and [58]; their complete external proofs were not re-audited here.

foundations.claim: Stable contraction, singularity geometry and cone quantifiers
foundations.disposition: Checked within the source's cited background; finite-entrance restriction isolated in FND-03
reasoning: For X in F^cu, the scaled normal contraction on E^s follows from ||Df_t|E^s|| / ||Df_t|span(X)|| <= ||Df_t|E^s|| / m(Df_t|F^cu), which is uniformly exponentially small by domination. No uniform positive lower bound for the speed is needed.

All singularities are assumed hyperbolic and hence isolated. The zero set of a continuous vector field on compact M is closed and compact; infinitely many zeros would have an accumulation zero, contradicting isolation. Therefore there are finitely many singularities and uniform minima over them are legitimate.
Proposition 2.14 supplies the Lorenz-like splitting with dim E^c=1 and Lambda intersect W^ss(sigma)={sigma}. This is an explicitly cited external structural result, not re-proved here.
The actual page-21 image shows the closure bar in B(Lambda)=closure(zeta(Lambda intersect Reg(X))); it is not an unclosed set. The closure was lost in plain text extraction.
Lemma 2.15 also follows directly from Lemma 2.13 and continuity of F^cu: every X(x_n) lies in F^cu(x_n), so every limiting flow line at sigma lies in F^cu(sigma)=E^c direct-sum E^u.
For finite entrance passages, Lemma 2.16 has the order alpha first, then r0, then a smaller r-bar, then every r<=r-bar. It does not give a radius independent of the requested cone aperture.

A positional E^c-cone estimate at the larger-ball entrance yields a flow-direction E^c-cone estimate after first narrowing the positional cone and then shrinking r0: X(exp_sigma v)=DX(sigma)v+o(|v|), E^c is invariant and its eigenvalue is nonzero. The transverse part is bounded by ||DX|| times the positional transverse component plus the small remainder, while the E^c part has a nonzero linear lower bound.
Lemma 2.15 alone does not imply an E^u exit-direction estimate. Such an estimate belongs to the later local-passage analysis, not to the statement reviewed here.

foundations.claim: Almost expansivity, existence of equilibrium states, and the periodic-orbit intersection wrapper
foundations.disposition: Cited statements and their use checked; one explicit local proof completion recorded
reasoning: Theorem 2.17 supplies almost expansivity for every invariant ergodic measure at one scale. The cited entropy-expansivity consequence yields upper semicontinuity of measure entropy, hence existence of equilibrium states for continuous potentials on the compact invariant set.
Theorem 2.18 provides positive topological entropy, and Theorem 2.19 combines cited generic structural results with the stable/unstable intersection conclusion.
For Theorem 2.19(3), if omega(x) avoids singularities, the cited intersection result and openness of transverse intersection give the desired result after pulling back along the flow.

The singular case needs the elementary split omitted from the printed argument: if x lies in W^s(sigma), use the same cited [28, Lemma 3.2] directly on x. One cannot in this case demand a regular z in omega(x), since omega(x) may be {sigma}.

Otherwise, infinitely deep visits produce entry times tending to infinity. A limit of the entry points is a regular point z in omega(x) intersect W^s(sigma); the cited intersection result applies at z and openness then applies at a forward iterate of x. Flow invariance pulls the intersection back to x.
This completion uses the scope of the external result exactly as the printed proof already does. No false conclusion of Theorem 2.19 is claimed.

foundations.claim: Pressure, decomposition, Bowen and improved CT hypotheses
foundations.disposition: Definitions, monotonicity and parameter roles checked; the full external CT theorem not independently re-proved
reasoning: Pressure on a segment collection is a limsup over real durations; this is distinct from simply choosing an arbitrary subsequence of integer durations. The later entropy construction must respect that limsup.

The weighted partition function is nonincreasing in the separation scale delta and nondecreasing in the potential-variation scale epsilon. The bound |Phi_epsilon-Phi_0|<=t Var(phi,epsilon) gives P(C,delta,epsilon)<=P(C,delta)+Var(phi,epsilon).
The variational principle uses measures invariant under the entire flow and entropy of its time-one map. This is the convention used in the corrected time-rescaling calculation.

A (P,G,S) decomposition requires a good core for every segment in D, with nonnegative real lengths summing to the original length. Having selected a candidate endpoint is insufficient unless its resulting core actually belongs to the particular G used in the CT theorem.
For G^M, the extra prefix and suffix have total length less than 2M. Their potential distortion is bounded by 2M Var(phi,epsilon), which verifies the displayed extension of the Bowen property.

The improved Theorem 3.3 retains both the large-scale Bowen condition and the pressure gap; it weakens the specification requirement to the good core G at one fixed scale. It still requires epsilon>=1000 Lip delta, where Lip controls both forward and backward times of length at most one.
A C1 flow on compact M has finite Lip. Extending a delta-shadowed core by less than one unit at either end multiplies spatial error by at most Lip, which explains the Lip delta scale in Remark 3.4.
The full existence/uniqueness implication of the improved CT criterion is quoted from [48], with the described Lipschitz adjustment. No independent complete proof of [48] is claimed.

foundations.claim: Pliss selection, scaled cu estimates and intersection counts
foundations.disposition: Core estimates checked with explicit corrected constants and the grid limitation in FND-01
reasoning: Lemma 4.2 is a genuine sequence concatenation statement: a suffix crossing the join splits into a suffix of the first block plus the whole second block. Both lower bounds add exactly. Its use for flows requires that the time samples line up across the join.
For v in F_N^cu(x), the area of the parallelogram generated by v and X(x) is |v||X(x)|. One-step sectional expansion and orthogonal projection give |v||X(x)| <= lambda_bar^(-1)|psi_1 v||X(x_1)|.
Substituting the speed scaling gives ||psi_-1^*|F_N^cu(y)|| <= lambda_bar^(-1)|X(y)|^2/|X(y_-1)|^2. The square of the speed ratio is essential.

Multiplying along the endpoint grid telescopes exactly to lambda_bar^(-N)|X(x_t)|^2/|X(x_(t-N))|^2. When x and x_t are outside W, the first ratio is uniformly bounded, and the remaining fractional time t-N in [0,1) contributes only a uniform short-time derivative constant.

A safe complete bound is C_W lambda_bar^(-N), with C_W=c_W^2 sup_(s in [-1,0])||Df_s||^2. Any fixed tilde-lambda in (1,lambda_bar) absorbs C_W once N is large enough, proving the claimed averaged expansion with N0 depending on W.

Use lambda_0 in (1,tilde-lambda), a uniform upper bound A for -log||psi_-1^*|| (for example from the scaled forward bound K1'), and the corrected non-strict Pliss count. This gives positive hyperbolic density independent of W.

For recurrence, apply Pliss to 1_(W^c) on exactly N endpoint-grid samples. The density is at least 1-beta_1/beta_0; it may be made arbitrarily close to one. It is not an unconditional count on N+1 eligible endpoints.
The positive-intersection argument is valid only for two subsets of the same finite grid. The explicit local repair in FND-01 preserves that common grid and accounts for every endpoint loss.

foundations.claim: Order of parameters needed for the CT pressure gap
foundations.disposition: Dependency order checked; does not certify the later full implementation
reasoning: With finitely many singularities and phi(sigma)<P(phi) for each, a positive amount b of singular mass forces a strictly lower pressure. If measures carry at least b mass in shrinking singular neighborhoods and their pressures tend to P(phi), weak-* compactness and entropy upper semicontinuity give an equilibrium state with singular mass at least b, contradicting the affine decomposition of entropy/pressure over singular atoms and the remaining invariant measure.

The intended order is beta_0 from the Bowen estimate, beta_1 from simultaneous Pliss selection, then r0 and a0 from the pressure-gap lemma at b=beta_1/2, then r and epsilon from the Bowen collection, followed by shrinking epsilon for almost expansivity and Var(phi,epsilon)<a0/2.

Only after epsilon is fixed is delta=epsilon/(1000 Lip) chosen; specification then produces CP_sigma(delta), and its allowed arbitrary open neighborhood U_Sing is subsequently chosen small in invariant-measure mass away from the singular balls.

The measure-zero assertion for CP_sigma minus singularities follows by recurrence for f_-1, since each of its regular points converges backward to sigma. Compactness and nested closed neighborhoods then justify the uniform small-mass choice for U_Sing.

This ordering avoids a circular dependence between the Bowen scale and specification scale, provided that the same corrected good collection satisfies both properties. The latter compatibility is part of the unresolved global repair, not a result of this check alone.

core.result: The compactness/upper-semicontinuity argument of Lemma5.4 is sound conditional on the cited entropy upper-semicontinuity. Finite hyperbolic singularities permit splitting a weak limit into point masses and a residual invariant measure. Positive mass on singularities and strict potential gap give strict pressure loss by entropy affinity. Lemma5.5 follows from backward Poincare recurrence because a nonstationary unstable-manifold point converges to the singularity backwards. Lemma5.6 uses nested compact neighborhoods and Portmanteau correctly.

The order beta0, beta1, singular-ball r0/a0, smaller r, Bowen epsilon, epsilon decrease for almost expansivity and potential oscillation, delta=epsilon/(1000Lip), CP(delta), then U_Sing is consistent with the stated quantifiers. The residence-time repair only further decreases r before epsilon is fixed and can enlarge N1 later. There is no parameter circularity detected in this sequence.

For B1, the segment outside Wr union U has length at most N1; hence the stated0.99 should be a lower bound valid for large t, and the needed0.6 beta1 follows. Prefix/suffix additions of bounded length do not affect limiting empirical masses or exponential growth rates. The margin a0/2 survives the modulus-of-continuity reduction of the second pressure scale. These conclusions are conditional on using an appropriate pressure-maximizing sequence, as corrected above.

The reduction from TheoremC is structurally correct conditional on the external Lorenz and robust periodic-manifold inputs. The classical Lorenz case uses an invariant contracting stable foliation, cone expansion and a crossing argument to obtain the quasi-u-section and dense stable manifold; flow invariance converts a weak-stable cross-section intersection into the required strong-stable intersection. Positive entropy then verifies the potential gap for zero potential. The generic theorem invokes Theorem2.19 and open-dense hyperbolic singularities. The quoted Tucker quantitative expansion/return statements and generic result were not independently read or certified; no error was manufactured from that limitation.

The graph cone condition gives |y-x|<=d_D(x,y)<=sqrt(1+alpha^2)|y-x| and hence Lemma6.3 with a larger linear-in-alpha constant. Conditional coordinate comparisons preserve Lemma6.4 as detailed above. Scaled Poincare maps are uniformly C1-close to their linear parts at a uniform scaled radius; a cutoff permits the cited Hadamard-Perron construction. Rescaling by |X(x)| produces the relative-size normal foliations. Their asserted invariance is only for integer iterates, which is material to the7.4 defect.

Lemmas6.7 and6.8 have distinct hypotheses: terminal E dominance gives backward E expansion and scaled shadowing; initial F dominance gives forward F expansion but no scaled-shadowing conclusion. The text correctly warns that6.8 is not obtained simply by reversing the flow. Their technical proofs lie in AppendixC and were assigned to the applications helper. No unsupported certification of those proofs is made here.

For a point already scaled-shadowed, the scaled Poincare maps have uniformly controlled derivatives. Along a forward cu-cone vector, the backward derivative estimate applies to its actual forward image; it does not assert backward invariance of the entire cu cone. Products at a cu-Pliss endpoint give lambda1=lambda0/(1+a)>1. To integrate the bound along a fake cu-leaf, one uses integer-step local invariance and chooses the original shadowing radius smaller by a fixed factor: cone coordinate upper estimates and arc-length comparison keep the F endpoint and connecting arcs within a fixed multiple of the scaled tube. The stable leg must be the segment from yF to y. This is a possible rigorous completion of the local integer-time length step; it does not fix arbitrary real-time changes of fake coordinates.

The base (K1')^(beta/(1-beta))/lambda1 tends to1/lambda1<1 as beta decreases, and beta^{-1}-1 diverges, so the smallness requirement7.7 is attainable before r and epsilon. Once large F-coordinate propagation and valid scaled-shadowing domains are available,7.9-7.11 cancel the speed factors correctly. The recurrence count with rounded endpoints may require additive constants (for example a denominator t-s1+1 rather than t-s1); these bounded losses can be absorbed by a stricter beta choice. This algebra does not establish the premise supplied by the false7.4 propagation.
